parity.evidence: Same TS rule under Node and ClearScript; synthetic projections, not AVM1 oracle

nodeBenchmark.limits: Node process measurements; includes JSON input parsing, document/HTML composition and JSON output. Does not include host scheduling, cache, IPC or Flash projection. Memory deltas include V8/JIT overhead and are not retained-object accounting.

clearScriptBenchmark.evidence: Linux ClearScript actual production bundle; no AVM1/Windows/CS6 evidence

evidenceLimits: The 1801 inputs are 1788 catalog baselines plus 13 synthetic supplied projections; no live AVM1 corpus was captured.
Node/ClearScript output equality tests the same TS rules on two hosts, not AS2-to-TS content equivalence.
The Linux cross-target compile is not a Windows runtime, WebView2, NativeHud, CS6 or SWF execution result.
Fake presentation surfaces do not validate real window visibility, scrolling, wheel routing, layout or pointer geometry.
Cold ClearScript initialization and RSS include first-process CLR/ClearScript/V8/JIT costs; they do not measure the marginal Tooltip isolate cost in a production process already running GameInput.
The Node and ClearScript benchmark runners have different warmup/pass schedules; their results are separate measurements, not a controlled runtime speed comparison.

Inventory/ItemUse write acknowledgement schemas contain no nested tooltip. The actual task test proves an independent committed consume acknowledgement is unchanged while a concurrent tooltip read fails; the generic enricher separately tests a nested-business-ack presentation failure.
No new GameInput engine/lock dependency or synchronous wait was introduced; GameInput frame timing under Windows was not measured.
PowerShell prepare/policy wiring was reviewed and the actual packer copy/hash regression ran on Linux; the full Windows release pipeline was not executed.
Unavailable content may remain in an existing Web success-response cache until that cache lifecycle invalidates the key; the UI text does not promise a same-key hover retry.
